newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap-Gas oil firm on physical support.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap-Gas oil firm on physical support.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps edged up at midday on Tuesday after strong physical buying support emerged late Monday, traders said.
"Gas oil received a lot of support yesterday because some people thought the market has bottomed," one trader said.
August swaps were last quoted at $21.75/$21.90 per barrel, up from Monday's $21.70/$21.80 per barrel, brokers said.
Brokers said August traded earlier at $21.80.
Traders said the buying interest emerged after the physical market failed to break the $20.00 per barrel earlier this month despite repeated attempts by several players to sell the market down.
After hovering at just under $20.00 per barrel in thin trading over the past week, physical prices rebounded after the last spate of purchases.
Traders said the physical market's resilience was also partly due to strong buying support in the swaps market by players who were trading the East-West spread.
On Monday four deals totalling 670,000 barrels were done between $20.90 and $21.20 per barrel on a free-on-board Singapore basis.
Traders said the mixed bag of buyers, who included a European major, a Dutch trader and a U.S. trader, revealed there was a fairly diverse set of buyers offering support.

Industry sources also observed the obvious absence of a Singapore trader among the buyers. The local trader and two other companies bought over 18 million barrels of gas oil over a two-month period beginning March 3.
The August-September contango in the fuel oil swaps market widened by about 25 cents to about 50 cents.
August was last quoted at $98.25/$99.25 and September edged up by 25 cents to $98.75/$99.75.
